experiments.name: dependent chain
experiments.init: li.d $r4, 1065353216; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1065353216; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr2, $r4; li.d $r5, -1; li.d $r6, 0
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 2000 --iters 300 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, 1065353216; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1065353216; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr2, $r4; li.d $r5, -1; li.d $r6, 0' --asm 'xvfdiv.s $xr0, $xr0, $xr2; xvpickve2gr.w $r4, $xr0, 0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr0, $r4'

latencies.notes: Data-dependent latency. Chain: tested op, then xvpickve2gr.w+and+or+xvreplgr2vr.w to restore the input pattern; the 9-cycle closure is subtracted (calibrated with vadd.b/xvadd.b). Swept 26 operand values including 0, powers of two, max, minnorm, maxsub, minsub, Inf and NaN: latency 11-17 cycles, CPI 6-9. The stored experiment uses 1.0. Measured on 2026-11-17 on LA464, core 0.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: xvfdiv.s $xr0, $xr8, $xr16; xvfdiv.s $xr1, $xr9, $xr17; xvfdiv.s $xr2, $xr10, $xr18; xvfdiv.s $xr3, $xr11, $xr19; xvfdiv.s $xr4, $xr12, $xr20; xvfdiv.s $xr5, $xr13, $xr21; xvfdiv.s $xr6, $xr14, $xr22; xvfdiv.s $xr7, $xr15, $xr23

throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, 1065353216; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr8, $r4; li.d $r4, 1065353216; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr9, $r4; li.d $r4, 1065353216; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr10, $r4; li.d $r4, 1065353216; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr11, $r4; li.d $r4, 1065353216; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr12, $r4; li.d $r4, 1065353216; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr13, $r4; li.d $r4, 1065353216; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr14, $r4; li.d $r4, 1065353216; xvreplgr2vr.w $xr15, $r4' --asm 'xvfdiv.s $xr0, $xr8, $xr16; xvfdiv.s $xr1, $xr9, $xr17; xvfdiv.s $xr2, $xr10, $xr18; xvfdiv.s $xr3, $xr11, $xr19; xvfdiv.s $xr4, $xr12, $xr20; xvfdiv.s $xr5, $xr13, $xr21; xvfdiv.s $xr6, $xr14, $xr22; xvfdiv.s $xr7, $xr15, $xr23'
throughput.notes: Data-dependent throughput, 8 independent lanes. CPI ranges 6-9 over the same 26-value sweep; the stored experiment uses 1.0.

notes: Latency model (measured with a 1-/2-/3-copy chain so the per-instruction latency is read off the increments, not the closure): 8 cycles when the operands are special (0, Inf or NaN on either side); 10 cycles when the divisor is a power of two (including 1.0); 22-23 cycles for a general divisor; up to 24 with a subnormal operand. Every lane of the vector divider runs in parallel and only the slowest lane matters (1 and 2 slow lanes both measure 24), so vfdiv.d/xvfdiv.d match the scalar numbers exactly. The 32-bit vector variants are slower (11 / 15 / 25-27) because 32-bit lanes are not fully parallel, the same behaviour as the integer .w divides. The stored experiment uses 1.0/1.0, i.e. the power-of-two-divisor path.
